text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- It is still not clear which flag, anthem or honour unit will be used at the reception of Pope John Paul II at Sarajevo airport on April 12, diplomatic sources say. Dayton peace agreement says that Bosnia must have common insignia for whole country but collective presidency is unable to agree.
- Session of Bosnia's central parliament, scheduled for April 8, is postponed to April 15 since deputies could not agree on daily working procedure.

- The mass return of Bosnian refugees from Germany, scheduled for beginning of April, will be postponed due to poor conditions in the country, experts from Bosnia and Germany agree. Only bachelors and couples without children will have to come back immediately.

- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation minister for energy, Izudin Kapetanovic, alleges Bosnian Serb republic to blame for whole debt of $12.4 million to Russian gas company. After Russian suppliers cut off gas deliveries, federation will think about different ways to import natural gas.

- The biggest obstacle for commercial cooperation between Bulgaria and Bosnia is the lack of free movement because Bosnian Serb republic charges 500 German marks for transit of a truck through Serb territory, Bulgarian ambassador to Bosnia, Marko Markov, says in an interview.
